title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Integrate with Microsoft Dataverse via APIs (Not using the standard Dataverse connector)
summary: This post demonstrates how to integrate Dynamics 365 Business Central with Microsoft Dataverse using direct REST APIs instead of the standard connector. It provides step-by-step guidance on authenticating with OAuth 2.0 and implementing GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE operations to synchronize data between Business Central and Dataverse tables.
key_points: Use OAuth 2.0 with Client Credentials grant type to authenticate with Dataverse APIs before performing any operations
Create custom tables in Business Central to store Dataverse data, using Guid fields as primary keys for proper association
Implement CRUD operations (Get, Insert, Update, Delete) using specific API endpoints and handling response headers like Prefer: return=representation
This approach doesn't require Dataverse licenses but requires custom development for each synchronized table
features: GET operation for reading Dataverse data

quotes.text: Using this way, users do not need a Dataverse license and can achieve real-time synchronization.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is the main advantage of this approach over standard connectors, making it cost-effective for organizations that need Dataverse integration without additional licensing.
